thread:
jess: Hey team, just triaging a customer escalation — they report intermittent 504s and duplicate side-effects when our Go SDK retries kick in. Customer says it only happens under high latency to our edge and when they cancel contexts client-side :grimacing:. Repro steps below.

jess: Repro (summarized):
1) Use SDK v0.9.2 with default http.Client.
2) Call an endpoint that takes ~2s occasionally.
3) They set a context with 1.5s deadline and also set client.Timeout = 3s.
4) On context cancel they sometimes observe the request retried and the server logs two identical POSTs.

jess: Here's the minimal-ish snippet they shared:
```go
client := &http.Client{Timeout: 3 * time.Second}
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, bytes.NewReader(payload))
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 1500*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
// SDK wraps this and does a retry loop on network errors / 5xx
```

alex: Thanks for the detail. A couple quick Qs: are they using http.Transport defaults or passing a custom Transport? Is the request body an io.ReadCloser that can't be rewound?

jess: They said "default transport" from net/http (no custom Transport) and the body is bytes.NewReader(payload) in their repro. They said SDK does retries automatically on 502/504 and on context deadline it sometimes triggers retry.

mira: Interesting. Two things come to mind:
- net/http behavior: if req.WithContext(ctx) is canceled, the RoundTripper returns an error, but if SDK's retry logic treats that as retriable it may reissue the request. If the body isn't reusable across retries (e.g., streaming body) it can misbehave. bytes.NewReader is rewindable so that probably isn't the root.
- client.Timeout vs ctx deadline: If client.Timeout is set, the http.Client wraps the request and cancels the context it created internally at deadline expiry which can interact badly with manual ctx cancel.

alex: Also check Transport.DisableKeepAlives and MaxIdleConnsPerHost — under load dead connections can cause extra network errors leading to retries. But duplicate side-effects after cancel suggests the first request actually reached the origin and the SDK retried, rather than a pure network failure.

jess: Customer logs show two POSTs with same idempotency header missing. They weren't setting an idempotency key in this case.

mira: That explains it. If the SDK treats certain errors as retriable but the caller didn't provide an idempotency key, retries can cause side effects. We should recommend configuring retry policy and using idempotency headers for non-idempotent endpoints. Also check the SDK version — we changed how we classify context cancellations in v0.10.0.

jess: They are on v0.9.2. Good catch. Any quick patch/workarounds we should give them?

alex: Actionable suggestions to send: 
- upgrade to SDK v0.10.x where we avoid retrying on ctx.Canceled / ctx.DeadlineExceeded in most cases (see changelog).
- prefer using either context deadlines OR client.Timeout, not both. If using ctx for fine-grained cancellation, leave client.Timeout=0 and rely on ctx.
- set an idempotency key header for POSTs that mutate state.
- if stuck on v0.9.x, set SDK retry policy to not retry on "context canceled" errors and reduce retryable status codes to exclude 504 for that route.
- tune http.Transport: Increase MaxIdleConnsPerHost, set IdleConnTimeout, ensure TLSHandshakeTimeout is sane. Example: 
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
```

mira: I'll add that we should ask them for a short pcap or tcpdump if they can, and the SDK debug logs (set REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1). Also request the exact sequence: whether both POSTs had different request IDs from our side or only server-side duplicates.

jess: Customer responded quickly: they can try v0.10.1 upgrade tomorrow and will add an idempotency key as a temporary band-aid. They attached SDK debug logs showing errors: 
```
net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```
and later a second POST shows up in server logs ~200ms after the cancel.

alex: That error string is coming from client.Timeout cancellation. So client.Timeout triggered, not the passed ctx. That explains why we saw two attempts: our retry saw a client.Timeout error (treated as transient) and retried.

mira: So immediate recommendation: remove client.Timeout or set it > ctx deadline and avoid treating client.Timeout as retriable. We'll open a support-safe snippet for them: 
```go
// prefer ctx for per-request deadlines
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 1500*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, bytes.NewReader(payload))
// use transport-tuned client without a global Timeout
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```

jess: I'll send that and propose the upgrade to v0.10.1 and adding idempotency keys. Also asking for pcap if they still see duplicates after upgrade.

deploy-bot: Note: SDK changelog entry added for v0.10.1 - "Do not retry on context cancellation caused by client timeout; improved retry classification" :white_check_mark:

alex: Perfect. I'll also file a quick follow-up GH issue to ensure our docs call out the client.Timeout vs ctx interaction and recommend idempotency for mutating endpoints.

jess: Thanks all, closing on this thread once customer confirms upgrade worked :thumbsup:
